## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pañcadīpadāyikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 15) is a verse narrative preserved in the Therīapadāna section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the past karmic deed of offering five lamps and the resulting spiritual attainments of a Buddhist nun (*therī*). SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 182 passages shared with 45 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Most prominently, it exhibits near-complete identity with the *Pañcadīpikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 9), sharing segments 0.3–27.1 at a 0.95 similarity score [DharmaNexus]. Large continuous verse portions are also found preserved in the commentary on the Therīgāthā (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, segments 9.1–23.1) and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, alongside recurring conventional verses shared with other poems in the Therīapadāna and Therāpadāna (such as Thi-Ap 14, Tha-Ap 558, Thi-Ap 11, and Tha-Ap 503) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-language reuse alignments with Sanskrit narrative literature (notably the *Kaṭhināvadāna*, *Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharājasūtra*, and *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna*) and Tibetan canonical translations (such as the *Candrottarādārikāvyākaraṇa-sūtra* and *Dānapāramitā-sūtra*), representing shared formulaic material [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
